To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Canadian forest product industry has been a net sink of CO2 for the period 1985-1989.

(a) in 1985-89, the Canadian forest sector (ecological and forest product sectors) was a net sink of 22.5 TgC yr-1; (b) in 1989 the forest product sector contained 0.84 PgC, of which 0.28 PgC was retained in Canada; (c) in 1987, the forest product sector accounted for about 6% of the total net exchange of the Canadian forest sector; and
(1) The forest product sector (FPS) of the Canadian forest sector is a significant net sink for atmospheric CO2, accounting for approximately 10% of the total net forest sector sink.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the C budget of the FPS, and with the potential to reduce the atmospheric CO2 emissions of the FPS by increasing the use of biomass C for energy.
the development of a national scale model that can be used to estimate the C budget of the Canadian FPS.
the C budget of the FPS, the C budget of forest ecosystems and the net atmospheric C exchange of the FPS and forest ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the absence of changes in the forest product sector, the total C budget of Canada's forest sector would be negative, with a net release of 0.8 Pg C yr ˛1.
the Canadian forest sector, as a whole, is a net sink for atmospheric carbon.
the Canadian FPS, on balance, has contributed to the mitigation of global warming by sequestering a significant amount of C in long‐lived products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the forest product sector has been a net sink of carbon since 1920.
the C budget of the Canadian FPS is in a net sink, with a net removal of C from the atmosphere of approximately 24 Tg C yr1 in 1989.
we have developed a tool that can be used to evaluate the C balance of the FPS, and to estimate the impact on the C balance of changes in forest management, harvest, and processing practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the forest product sector has a large impact on the carbon balance of the forest sector, and that the impact is positive.
, although the FPS is a small part of the total forest C budget, its contribution to the net C balance can be significant.
the forest products sector is a net sink for atmospheric CO2, and that the sector can be managed to maximize this benefit.
